architecture.mechanism: Anisotropic particle shape and induced Marangoni flows can shift colloid deposition from heterogeneous (ring-like) to uniform during drying, with increased CMM bending rigidity reinforcing even coverage.
architecture.intervention: Apply a self-assembling colloidal protective topcoat containing ellipsoidal microparticles and a trace surfactant to the blade leading edge before service windows; as the carrier solvent evaporates, particle shape plus Marangoni recirculation drive uniform coating deposition to form a wear-resisting blanket rather than edge-localized deposits.
architecture.expected_effect: More uniform abrasion-resistant layering on the leading edge, reducing localized erosion severity and mitigating the 4–6% annual energy production loss between scheduled repairs.
architecture.falsification_test: Spray-coat representative composite coupons with and without ellipsoidal particles plus surfactant, dry under controlled evaporation, expose both sets to rainfall/hail impact simulations, and show statistically greater edge-localized erosion or coating thinning on the spherical/surfactant-absent coupons.
